title: Agentic Coding is a Trap | Lars Faye
summary: Argues fully agentic, orchestration-style coding atrophies the very skills needed to supervise agents and adds vendor and cost dependence, recommending LLMs as secondary tools with the developer still writing much of the code.

assertions.quote: The use of coding agents is actively diminishing the very skills needed to effectively manage the coding agents.

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.

assertions.quote: only a skilled developer who's thinking critically, and comfortable operating at the architectural level, can spot issues in the thousands of lines of generated code

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.

assertions.quote: a higher level of ambiguity is not a higher level of abstraction.

verdicts.note: A historical framing; the analogy is debated because LLM output is non-deterministic, unlike compilers.

assertions.quote: Contrary to the current narrative that is being espoused, we didn’t necessarily need to write code faster.

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: you cannot understand code without engaging with it.

verdicts.note: Naur's theory-building view and early studies of AI-assisted teams support loss of understanding as a real risk, but there is no measurement yet showing it outweighs technical debt.

assertions.quote: Vendor lock-in for individuals and entire teams (Claude Code outages have already had entire teams at a stand-still).

verdicts.note: Outages of hosted agents have stalled teams that rely on them, but most teams can still code without the agent; the dependency is real but usually recoverable.

assertions.quote: Model providers are heavily subsidized, and the models themselves are built on shifting sands.

verdicts.note: Heavy users clearly consume more compute than flat fees cover, which is why vendors added weekly limits; whether plans are below cost on average is not public.

assertions.quote: I never generate more than I can review in a sitting.

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: forced mandates and hype around token usage across organizations is demonstrating as such.

verdicts.note: Reports of token-maxing and resentment support it, but some mandated rollouts (e.g. Shopify, Coinbase) report adoption gains; evidence is anecdotal either way.

assertions.quote: when used responsibly, they can be a stellar tool for learning and upskilling.

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 study found high scorers used AI for conceptual questions and explanations while low scorers delegated; small sample and a single learning task.
